summary: We developed Astro Health, a health monitoring app for astronauts on long-duration missions, available as a website and a Windows desktop app. On missions far from Earth, astronauts must spot changes in their own health, and early detection can stop small changes from becoming emergencies. Astro Health brings vitals, symptoms, radiation dose, and cabin conditions into one dashboard and compares every reading to the astronaut’s own baseline instead of Earth averages. It scores risks for the cardiovascular, immune, bone, and behavioral systems, tracks how many days each symptom has lasted, and escalates persistent symptoms with clear advice, including when to contact the crew medical officer. A daily log and trend charts show how health changes over time. The app works fully offline, so monitoring continues when communication with Earth is lost. It addresses the challenge by helping astronauts gather indicators, evaluate their health, and act on it. This prototype uses only demo data. With the help of Claude by Anthropic.
details:
Astro Health is a health monitoring app for astronauts on long-duration missions, where help from Earth can be delayed or unavailable. The astronaut logs a daily check-in covering heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, temperature, sleep, mood, stress, social contact, exercise, radiation dose, and cabin conditions (CO₂, humidity, temperature, noise). The app compares every reading to that astronaut’s own recent baseline, not to Earth averages, because spaceflight changes the body.

It then scores four health risks (cardiovascular, immune, bone and muscle, behavioral health) and four stressors (radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, a closed environment). A readiness score, colored bars, and status indicators show the result at a glance, with a plain-language suggested action for each. A symptom tracker counts how many days each symptom has lasted. Persistent symptoms escalate, with advice on when to contact the crew medical officer. A daily log with trend charts shows how health changes over time, and a short summary can be prepared to send to the ground team.

Benefits and impact:

On long missions, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for spotting health changes in themselves. Astro Health helps them gather indicators, evaluate their status, and act early, before small changes become emergencies. It works fully offline, so monitoring continues when communication with Earth is lost.

How it was built:

The app uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It is available as a website, hosted on Netlify, and as a Windows desktop app built with Electron. The desktop version can also show live PC information such as CPU, memory, and battery. Data is saved locally on the user’s device, which keeps health data private.

What makes it creative:

We built a dark space themed interface with animations, a readiness ring, and live indicators so health data is easy to read quickly. Personal baselines, duration-based symptom escalation, and offline-first design were chosen to fit the astronaut scenario.
